cards.back: If $b^n = a$, then $b$ is an nth root of $a$, written as $\sqrt[n]{a}$ or $a^{1/n}$. $n$ is the index (integer >1).
cards.front: Define an [[kw:nth root]] of a number $a$.

cards.back: One. Because the index 5 is odd, every real number has exactly one real nth root. $\sqrt[5]{-32} = -2$.
cards.front: How many real fifth roots does $-32$ have?

cards.back: Two: $\sqrt[4]{81} = \pm 3$. When the index $n$ is even and $a>0$, there are two real nth roots (positive and negative).
cards.front: How many real fourth roots does $81$ have?
What is the principal fourth root of 16?
cards.back: The positive root: $\sqrt[4]{16} = 2$. When $n$ is even, the principal root is the positive one.
$x^{3/5}$. The numerator of the exponent is the power (3), the denominator is the index (5).
cards.front: How do you write $\sqrt[5]{x^3}$ using a rational exponent?

cards.back: $16^{3/2} = (\sqrt{16})^3 = 4^3 = 64$. Take the square root first, then cube.
Enter 9^(1/5) to get about 1.55. Without parentheses, 9^1/5 gives 1.8 because the calculator computes $9^1$ then divides by 5.
cards.front: When evaluating $9^{1/5}$ on a calculator, why must you use parentheses?

cards.back: Take the fifth root of both sides: $x = \sqrt[5]{32} = 2$. Since the exponent is odd, there is exactly one real solution.
Take the fourth root (even, so $\pm$): $x-3 = \pm \sqrt[4]{21}$. Then $x = 3 \pm \sqrt[4]{21} \approx 5.14 \text{ or } 0.86$.
No. An even power of a real number is always nonnegative, so it can't equal a negative number. No real sixth root of a negative.
cards.front: Does $x^6 = -64$ have real solutions? Why or why not?

cards.back: The annual depreciation rate $r$ using the declining balance method. $C$ = original cost, $S$ = salvage value, $n$ = useful life in years.

cards.front: If a machine costs $\$50{,}000$, salvage value $\$8{,}000$, and life 10 years, find $r$.
Write $\sqrt[3]{-64}$ both as a radical and as a rational exponent.
cards.back: Radical: $\sqrt[3]{-64} = -4$. Rational exponent: $(-64)^{1/3} = -4$. Since the index is odd, the single real root is negative.
